channel.title: Compositions on Hsing-An Lee
channel.description: Hsing-An Lee is a recorder player and composer.

item.title: Polygatari - 祭り(Matsuri)
item.description:
A contemporary recorder work blending jazz, electronic music, and Japanese folk-inspired elements. This is one of my most representative works.
This work received Second Prize and the Best Composition Award at Open Recorder Days Amsterdam 2023.
item.content:encoded:
A contemporary recorder work blending jazz, electronic music, and Japanese folk-inspired elements. This is one of my most representative works.

This work received Second Prize and the Best Composition Award at Open Recorder Days Amsterdam 2023.

In this piece, I used the DAW Reason as my creative tool. Inspired by odd-meter music, I experimented with an uneven seven-beat rhythmic structure.
In live performance, the piece combines live looping with a pre-programmed track. The recorder sound is also routed into the computer, where effects open up a wider range of timbral possibilities.

Polygatari - 祭り(Matsuri) Monogatari (物語) means “story” in Japanese. Just as monophony evolves into polyphony, I wanted my monogatari to evolve as well.
Matsuri (祭り) means festival.

As the third piece in the Polygatari series, this is probably a festival taking place under a full moon, somewhere below the castle. The people here move with a staggering yet light step; he wears a white amoeba-patterned shirt, he wears a haori, he is restrained, yet free.
And he is very handsome.

 Open Recorder Days Amsterdam 2023 Competition
 Recorder & Electronic: Hsing-An Lee
 Composer: Hsing-An Lee

item.title: あたらよ(Atarayo)
item.description:
A trio for two clarinets and piano

item.content:encoded:
A trio for two clarinets and piano

あたらよ (Atarayo) is a Japanese word for “a night so beautiful that one feels reluctant to let it end.”

While studying composition, I often find myself drawn to many musical styles and theories. I consider myself fairly open to different kinds of artistic work; early music, folk music, classical music, jazz, contemporary music, and electronic music can all make me spend a great deal of time studying them.

At the same time, this makes me think about what the music I “like” actually is, and what kinds of sounds feel beautiful to me. I tried to use more of the elements I am drawn to, including fourths, extended chords, and borrowed chords from more distant keys; these less obvious tonal shifts seem to interest me more.

Through music, this piece tries to record the atarayo that drew me into composition, while also using a more elusive sense of tonality to create a night one would be reluctant to see end.

item.description:
A short piece written for recorder quintet, imitating the lively and energetic atmosphere of Chinese New Year.
Blending fantasy colors with folk-inspired musical language, the piece uses strong rhythmic patterns and non-functional harmony to create a sound world with a sense of Eastern mystery and celebration.

item.title: Relative Deprivation
item.description:
A trio for two clarinets and piano
Relative deprivation is a subjective psychological phenomenon: after comparing oneself with others, or with one&rsquo;s own expectations, one feels deprived because reality falls short of the object of comparison.
Like a carefully written essay missing its final period, the gradual indifference of a partner in a relationship, or the realization that one&rsquo;s hard-earned result still falls short of someone with extraordinary talent, people may only become more aware of what they truly want at the moment when an expectation is taken away.
item.content:encoded:
A trio for two clarinets and piano

Relative deprivation is a subjective psychological phenomenon: after comparing oneself with others, or with one’s own expectations, one feels deprived because reality falls short of the object of comparison.
Like a carefully written essay missing its final period, the gradual indifference of a partner in a relationship, or the realization that one’s hard-earned result still falls short of someone with extraordinary talent, people may only become more aware of what they truly want at the moment when an expectation is taken away.

In this piece, I tried to create expectation in different ways, then remove it just as it seems about to arrive. Through this process, I hoped listeners might become aware of the sound they were waiting for, and experience a kind of relative deprivation within the music itself.

item.title: Dialog
item.description:
A duet for two recorders
This work received Second Place with Distinction in the Professional Duo/Trio category of the Taiwan International Recorder Festival Competition. As both composer and performer, I often encounter the same problem: no matter how I try to avoid it, the music I make always carries a certain accent. Especially on an instrument I know well, the act of composing almost determines its way of speaking, as if that were the only possible &ldquo;authorial intention.&rdquo;
item.content:encoded:
A duet for two recorders

This work received Second Place with Distinction in the Professional Duo/Trio category of the Taiwan International Recorder Festival Competition.

As both composer and performer, I often encounter the same problem: no matter how I try to avoid it, the music I make always carries a certain accent. Especially on an instrument I know well, the act of composing almost determines its way of speaking, as if that were the only possible “authorial intention.”

This becomes even more awkward in a piece centered on “dialogue”; I cannot make it sound as though I am simply talking to myself.

Through my partner’s interpretation, the piece gained another layer of meaning: understanding the author, understanding the music, and then speaking it with one’s own accent. Through music, the idea of a “dialogue” becomes clearer.

 Taiwan Recorder Festival 2024 Competition
 Recorder: Hsing-An Lee, I-Chen Lin
 Composer: Hsing-An Lee

item.title: Gurenge (arranged for recorder quartet)
item.description:
LiSA&rsquo;s &ldquo;Gurenge&rdquo; is the opening theme song of the anime Demon Slayer. This version is arranged for recorder quartet.
While keeping the original song&rsquo;s clear melodic profile and forward drive, the arrangement redistributes the melody, accompaniment, and rhythmic functions across the ensemble.
The arrangement makes use of the recorder ensemble&rsquo;s clear layers of sound and agile articulation, aiming to present the original song&rsquo;s strong rhythmic character and dramatic tension.

item.title: Is There Still Anything That Love Can Do? (arranged for recorder quartet)
item.description:
RADWIMPS&rsquo; &ldquo;Is There Still Anything That Love Can Do?&rdquo; is one of the theme songs from the animated film Weathering with You. This version is arranged for recorder quartet.
The arrangement preserves the original song&rsquo;s long, narrative melodic line while reworking the harmonic and accompaniment layers among the four parts.
In arranging the piece, I focused on the recorder&rsquo;s transparency and singing quality, hoping to present the original song&rsquo;s gradually building emotional tension and sense of hope within a more compact ensemble setting.

item.title: Lady of the Pier (arranged for recorder quartet)
item.description:
&ldquo;Lady of the Pier&rdquo; is a song from the game Devotion, arranged here for recorder quartet.
With its strong retro popular-song character and dramatic atmosphere, this version keeps the original melody and nostalgic tone while redistributing the harmony and rhythmic functions among the four recorder parts.
In the arrangement, I focused on the recorder&rsquo;s plain, singing quality, hoping to use a relatively pure recorder ensemble texture to present the tenderness and slight melancholy of the original song.
